draft.title: Natural hazards and disasters
card: An event in nature that could harm people or property. Examples are cyclones, floods and earthquakes.
A hazard becomes a disaster when it causes major damage or loss of life that a community cannot cope with on its own.
The same hazard can be a disaster in one place and not in another. It depends on how many people are in the way and how well they can cope.
A hazard that strikes empty land, or a place well prepared for it, may cause little harm. It stays a hazard and does not become a disaster.
draft.remember: A hazard is the possible harm. A disaster is when a community cannot cope with the harm alone.

a.q: What is the difference between a natural hazard and a disaster?
opts: A disaster is a hazard a community cannot cope with alone
A disaster is a hazard that happens in a large city
A hazard is a human event and a disaster is a natural one
A hazard is a small event and a disaster is a big one
a.why: A hazard only could cause harm. It becomes a disaster when the damage or loss of life is more than the community can handle alone. Size alone is not the test: a big event in an empty or well prepared area may not be a disaster.
a.clue: Think about whether the community can cope by itself.

b.q: An earthquake of the same strength strikes two places. In a remote desert, no one is hurt and nothing is damaged. In a crowded town, many homes fall and people need outside help. What can be said?
opts: Both are hazards, but only the town's is a disaster
Both are disasters, because the strength was the same
Neither is a hazard, because earthquakes are natural
Only the desert one is a hazard, as it was not in a town
b.why: Both events are natural hazards because they could harm people or property. Only the town's event caused major damage that the community could not cope with alone, so it is a disaster. Strength is the same, but the harm and the ability to cope are not.
b.clue: Both events are hazards. Which one overwhelmed a community?

a.best: A disaster is a hazard a community cannot cope with alone

b.best: Both are hazards, but only the town's is a disaster
